text:
Tomas: Hi folks — quick onboarding payroll/benefits logistics before I start Mon. Two weird ones: 1) My lease broker charged a finders fee to my roommate's card  can company reimburse me if I pay them back? 2) My offer mentions a "move stipend (taxable)" vs "relocation reimbursements"  how are those handled on paycheck/1099? Also: will short-term disability enrollment happen automatically or do I need to opt in?

Lin (People Ops): Welcome Tomas! :wave: Short answers: reimbursements require receipts and must be in your name (or you must show proof you reimbursed your roommate). Stipends usually show up as taxable income and are paid through payroll as a one-time taxable benefit. For STD  you usually get automatic enrollment into basic employer-paid STD and have the option to buy-up for additional coverage during initial benefits enrollment window.

Harper (Benefits): Hey Tomas  for the broker fee: if you reimburse your roommate and submit a receipt showing you paid them (e.g., Venmo/Bank transfer screenshot + the original broker invoice), we can process it as a relocation expense, subject to policy limits. Please attach a short note explaining the chain of payment.

Harper (Benefits): About stipend vs reimbursement: relocation reimbursements (itemized receipts) are non-payroll reimbursements and paid via finance (non-taxable if they meet IRS moving expense rules, rare). Stipends are typically processed on payroll as taxable income and will appear on your W-2. We can confirm exact tax treatment if you share the offer code.

Tomas: Got it. If I want the broker fee reimbursed non-taxably, is there a preferred flow (i.e., have finance pay the roommate directly)?

Harper (Benefits): Finance can issue payment directly to a third party in exceptional cases, but we need manager approval + signed vendor invoice showing the roommate as payee with a company approval memo. Easier path: reimburse you after you document you reimbursed roommate. Either way finance needs the invoice + proof.

Nina (Payroll): Clarifying payroll bits: taxable stipend will be included on the next payroll after HR flags it. That means federal/state withholding applies, and it will show in your YTD gross. For reimbursements through finance, payroll is not involved unless it's a taxable reimbursement. If you want a run-down on how it will affect your net pay, DM me and I can run the numbers for your next pay date.

Tomas: Thanks  last Q on holidays/pay schedule: there's a company holiday the Friday after I start. Will that delay my first net pay if payroll cutoff hits?

Lin (People Ops): Holidays don't delay payroll runs, payroll runs per schedule. If payday falls on a holiday, payroll processes earlier as usual and you'll still be paid for company-observed holiday from day one. If you have bank cutoff concerns, ping Nina and she can confirm bank transfer schedule.

Onboard Bot: Checklist status: benefits enrollment link sent; payroll provisioning complete; payroll cutoff for first pay: 48h from payroll run. Link: https://onboard.redwood.example/checklist/tomas-1776

Tomas: Perfect. I'll pay my roommate today and submit Venmo + broker invoice to finance. How should I label the expense in Expensely?

Harper (Benefits): In Expensely choose expense type "Relocation - Third Party" and put note: "Broker fee reimbursed to roommate - <roommate name> - offer <offerID>". Upload Venmo/bank transfer screenshot and original broker invoice. We'll route to finance and payroll as needed.

Nina (Payroll): FYI: if you elect 401(k catch-up or pre-tax commuter midmonth, contributions may be prorated on first paycheck. We can walk through it if you plan changes.

Tomas: Appreciate it all, will submit now. See you Monday! :tada:
